request.deadline: 18-month transition and operations period, with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Legally establish a not-for-profit entity or sign a host-organization agreement under the preliminary board.
Publish technical transition architecture and migration plan for community review.
Hold a board election via on-chain voting under published rules and install the elected board.
Serve all public API traffic for mainnet, preview, and preprod from the new stack.
Transfer Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to the governing entity.
Open a public consultation and publish a long-term sustainability proposal.
Operate the public API at a minimum 99% monthly uptime SLA and publish quarterly technical and budget reports.
request.recipient: Input Output / Blockfrost transition project, with Intersect administering treasury management and delivery assurance as described.
request.what: Transition Blockfrost into a free, community-governed public good under an independent not-for-profit, including 18 months of transition and operations funding.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is presented as a hosted REST interface that lets Cardano developers read from and interact with the blockchain without running their own infrastructure or node.
The proposal states that Blockfrost developer survey adoption grew from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025 and links to the Cardano Foundation survey pages for each year.
The proposal states that Blockfrost served 781k unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, nearly 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data last month.
The proposal states that in most Cardano epochs more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost.
The proposal states that more than 100 Icebreakers have joined the decentralized Blockfrost operator effort.
The proposal claims 90% of Cardano traffic served through the Blockfrost API comes from the free tier and that the commercial model cannot sustainably finance that public-good operation.
The proposal commits to transfer Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets to the community-governed not-for-profit entity as part of the transition.

The proposed governance model has a five-seat board with four seats for open-source infrastructure development entities and one community seat, preceded by a named preliminary board and an IOG non-voting advisory seat for the first year.
The requested budget is 9,832,979 ADA, calculated as 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, with 79.1% for staffing, 19.3% for operations and infrastructure, and 1.6% for legal and accounting.

The proposal states that project delivery will be governed by an off-chain legal contract, milestone acceptance, Intersect delivery assurance, third-party assurance, and treasury management smart contracts with listed addresses and oversight participants.

summary: The document requests 9,832,979 ADA to move Blockfrost from a commercial service into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, with claimed high adoption, staged legal and technical transition milestones, public reporting, IP transfer, and assurance mechanisms, but several key usage and dependency claims are asserted rather than evidenced within the document.
